$comment: 🎯️ Local-space extents a screen-space hit test must use for one instance's mesh, declared neutrally. A URL-backed mesh record carries no inline `data` (the guest publishes {id, url} for every catalogue representation), so the corners have to come from the loaded GLB's own bounds; only while that GLB is still loading may the unit cube stand in. Ticket 26/09/02/PUZZLE-3D-END-TO-END wave B46.

cases.name: inline mesh data wins over everything
a url-backed mesh uses the loaded GLB's recorded extents
a url-backed mesh whose GLB has not loaded yet falls back to the unit cube
a mesh with neither data nor url falls back to the unit cube
an empty inline mesh is not geometry and does not shadow the recorded extents

projectedPick.$comment: 🖱️ The nearest projected AABB containing the click wins. `a` is a small box the click misses when it is sized as a unit cube and hits when it is sized from the GLB — the exact difference measured on the 180-object Nakagin tower (containing=0 before, containing=14 after).

leftoverOverlay.$comment: 🎯️ The host's leftover overlay exists to make a pick visible before the guest's own lane answers. `activeObjectId` is a single field several readers take instead of the list (gumball target, Inspection focus, `data-selection-json`), so it has to travel with the ids the overlay supplies.

cases.name: overlay ids carry the active object
an active object the overlay still names does not move
an active object the overlay dropped is replaced
an empty overlay leaves the guest's own answer alone
